description: A roleplay server's dice roll, thrown where it can be seen: the chat line is held back, a die appears, you throw it by hand, and it lands on the number the server rolled.

mods.name: Roleplayer's Dice
mods.description: Turns a roleplay server's /dice command into a Baldur's Gate style throw: the result is held out of the chat, a die appears, you click, it tumbles, and the number it lands on is the one the server rolled – with the verdict spelled out underneath. Client side only; the server is never told it exists.

releases.notes:
### The heading now takes all the room there is

1.1.1 pinned the wrapped heading to the top edge so no row could be drawn off it. That kept the words on screen and paid for it in words: a die sitting high up left space for a single row, the rest of the sentence became an ellipsis, and the gap between the words and the die sat empty while it happened.

The block now comes down towards the die when the top edge is what it ran into, as far as the die itself. That is some four more rows, and they read perfectly well over it – the words carry their own dark halo and a die is a flat pale shape behind them. The ordinary gap above the die is still where the heading sits; coming down is only what happens when the alternative is losing the text.

Whatever the space cannot hold even then is still cut with an ellipsis. If your die sits near the top of the screen and you want more of a long line, raise **Rows of words** or narrow **Width of the words** – narrower rows mean more of them fit.

Minecraft 1.20.5–1.21.11, Fabric.

releases.notes:
The first release.

One jar for **1.20.5 – 1.21.11**. Client side only; the server is never told the mod is there.

- Holds the result line back, throws a die for it, and lets the line through once the die has landed on the number the server actually rolled.
- Throw it by clicking, or hold the button and throw it by hand: the camera freezes, the die follows the pointer a moment late, leans into the drag, and goes where the hand was going.
- d4, d6, d8, d12 and d20, every face a different number, the numerals engraved in the plane of the face they sit on.
- A colour per player, taken from their UUID – the same colour Voice Subtitles gives their speech.
- Other people's rolls come up small and out of the way, unless you would rather they did not.
- Escape or a hit puts the die away at once and prints the result.
- Everything the mod reads and everything it draws is a setting, including the pattern it recognises a roll by – see the description for how to write one for your own server's wording.
